### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s).

**18** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57445a699810a0545d8b3a7649a77327d47fb18b`.

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `created_at (literal, 49 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **6** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57445a699810a0545d8b3a7649a77327d47fb18b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `932104ded86e28f8ebb6290710dba99ca507c0ea` — the merge of head `2fb042637378ff461bd0101f54ed9f4bb908c55b` into base `57445a699810a0545d8b3a7649a77327d47fb18b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 932104ded86e28f8ebb6290710dba99ca507c0ea && git checkout 932104ded86e28f8ebb6290710dba99ca507c0ea
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 57445a699810a0545d8b3a7649a77327d47fb18b 2fb042637378ff461bd0101f54ed9f4bb908c55b && git checkout -B drift-repro 57445a699810a0545d8b3a7649a77327d47fb18b && git merge --no-ff 2fb042637378ff461bd0101f54ed9f4bb908c55b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57445a699810a0545d8b3a7649a77327d47fb18b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 57445a699810a0545d8b3a7649a77327d47fb18b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · repo:objectstack#3 · head 2fb04263 · 2026-11-24T13:21Z

L1 read of #36976 (card #36959, p1) at `2fb042637378ff461bd0101f54ed9f4bb908c55b`. Clause-② no and Metadata-protocol none, both true: the `q` accept set is unchanged and only what it matches widens, on a non-spec surface. NOT governed, 537 changed lines. `l1-face` is clean. No contract review is owed by surface. I read the visibility invariant myself, below, and judged that it does not need one.

**Against the card.** `buildRequestWhere` keeps its four machine arms and the snapshot arm, unchanged with `freeTextMayMatchSnapshot`. It adds `servedTextArms`: the process label, object label, requester name and record title, each resolved first, the way this caller is served it, into an `$in` over machine values. The filer's terms are pinned on real ObjectQL over SqlDriver: 商机 matches, 出差 finds a row once although it sits in two of its labels, the object filter is set, and `countRequests` agrees with the list. The machine-column controls still match.

**The invariant (read hardest).** A request is never found by text the same caller is not served.
- **Title.** `recordsTitledWith` reads under `SYSTEM_CTX` and decides with `titleAsServed(rec, displayField, readable)`, where `readable` is `servedFields` asked as the caller. That is the same function, read the same way, as the serve path's `titlesAsServed` (`resolveSubjectDisplays`), so it is no wider than what is served. The pushed-down `$contains` is limited to title candidates in the served set and is only a superset filter: a record whose `name` wins `pickTitle` is not found through a `title` field that holds the term. The deleted-record snapshot fallback is not searched, which narrows and is stated.
- **Process label.** A picked translation matches via `process_name $in`. The stored `process_label $contains` is limited to flows with no pick, so a reader shown the translation is not found by the stored text. This is pinned, and the ablation reds it.
- **Object label and requester.** These use the same pair and the same resolver (`readerLabels`, then `objectLabelOf`, and `resolveUserNames`) that set `object_label` and `submitter_name`.
- **Scope.** The scope read takes machine columns only and is never served. The participant narrowing still applies to the whole predicate afterwards. A failed read or an unresolved label adds no arm, so the search narrows and never widens. Every arm's value set is non-empty, and the `$or` keeps its machine arms.
- The masked and unreadable title pins have a readable control. Moving `status` above the free-text block feeds the scope read and leaves the final predicate unchanged.

**Changeset.** It names `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` at patch, and each sentence holds, including the case-sensitivity and deleted-record sentences.

**Nits (none block).**
- N1. The scope window is `SERVED_TEXT_SCOPE_CAP = 5,000`, newest first, with a `warn`. In a tenant past that, labels of older requests are not searched. The machine arms still are. It is stated in the body and the code. A follow-up card is worth filing if a tenant reaches it.
- N2 (SQL first). Labels are resolved in the app, not by a join, and the reason is given: each label is computed at serve time (translation picks, the user-name resolver, field-level redaction), so none is a column the predicate can test as served. Titles and the stored process label still push down. Accepted.
- N3. Each search adds a scope read, a `sys_user` read and one title read per subject object. The body states this, and it is bounded.
- N4. Matching stays case-sensitive (`$contains`), like the existing arms. It is out of scope and noted.
- The deviation (three pushes before the first overlap-check, which then read clean) is a process slip only.

**Mechanical.** All-checks: 37 success · 16 expected skips · 0 failed · 0 pending. Floor checks are green, `mergeable_state` is clean, and `Fixes #36959` delivers the card.

Every open finding is a nit. **ACCEPT**, ordinary queue landing.
